Nvidia Supplier / Flex.role: Diversified electronics manufacturing services firm whose cloud/data-center segment builds AI server and power infrastructure; it sits in AI-infra as a low-margin, cyclical contract manufacturer with modest moat and meaningful exposure to hyperscaler capex swings.

Micron peer / Analog Devices.role: ADI is a diversified high-performance analog and mixed-signal leader serving industrial, automotive, and communications markets; AI exposure is indirect (power management, data-center signal chain), making it a quality cyclical rather than a pure AI play.

NXP Semiconductors.role: NXP is a leading automotive and industrial semiconductor maker whose edge-processing, microcontroller, and connectivity chips enable on-device AI, but its revenue is cyclical and tied to auto/industrial demand rather than the data-center AI boom, placing it mid-quality with moderate capex sensitivit

Microchip Technology.role: Microchip supplies microcontrollers, analog, and FPGAs with growing edge-AI inference capability; it sits as a cyclical AI-infra name recovering from an inventory-correction downcycle with modest near-term growth and moderate moat in embedded markets.

ON Semiconductor.role: ON is a power/analog chipmaker levered to autos and industrial with a growing but modest data-center power delivery angle; its AI exposure is real but secondary to cyclical end-markets, so earnings are cyclical and the moat is moderate.

GlobalFoundries.role: Specialty foundry focused on differentiated non-leading-edge nodes (RF, power, automotive, IoT); modest AI exposure and cyclical end markets make it a mid-quality, moderately durable infrastructure play rather than a leading-edge AI beneficiary.

Entegris.role: Supplies ultra-high-purity materials, filtration, and advanced delivery systems essential to semiconductor fabrication; recurring consumables tied to wafer starts give durable demand but exposure to fab utilization cycles keeps it moderately cyclical.

MKS Instruments.role: MKS supplies critical subsystems (vacuum, RF power, photonics, lasers) and materials for semiconductor fabrication and advanced packaging; it sits in AI-infra as a diversified picks-and-shovels enabler but carries cyclical wafer-fab-equipment exposure and meaningful debt from the Atotech acquisition

Axcelis Technologies.role: Supplier of ion implantation systems for semiconductor fabs, with heavy exposure to the cyclical mature-node and power/automotive (SiC) markets rather than leading-edge AI logic, making revenue volatile and dependent on fab capex cycles.

Photronics.role: Photronics is a leading merchant supplier of photomasks essential to semiconductor and flat-panel manufacturing; it sits in AI-infra as a critical but cyclical upstream input with a duopolistic merchant position yet modest growth and exposure to fab capex cycles.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor is the leading maker of advanced probe cards used to test semiconductor wafers, benefiting from HBM/AI chip complexity but exposed to cyclical semiconductor test capex and customer concentration.

Cohu.role: Cohu supplies semiconductor test handlers, contactors, and inspection equipment; it sits in AI-infra as a back-end test play but is highly cyclical and tied to discretionary semi capex, limiting durability.

Ichor Holdings.role: Supplies gas and chemical fluid delivery subsystems to semiconductor capital equipment OEMs, so demand is tightly levered to volatile WFE capex cycles with modest moat and thin margins.

Ultra Clean Holdings.role: UCTT builds subsystems, modules, and provides contamination-control services for wafer-fab equipment makers; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical, low-margin supplier highly leveraged to semicap spending with modest moat and thin earnings durability.

Veeco Instruments.role: Veeco supplies deposition, laser annealing, and ion-beam process equipment to semiconductor and compound-semi fabs; it rides AI/advanced-node capex but is a mid-tier, cyclical equipment name with niche rather than dominant positioning, hence moderate growth and capex sensitivity.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Supplier of magnetic position/current sensors and power ICs heavily exposed to automotive (EV/ADAS) and industrial end-markets; cyclical demand and auto-chip inventory swings make earnings volatile despite solid niche share, so it sits as a mid-quality cyclical semiconductor name only loosely tied t

Power Integrations.role: Power Integrations designs high-voltage power-conversion semiconductors for appliances, industrial, and consumer markets; it sits as a quality-cyclical with solid niche dominance but limited direct AI leverage and exposure to broad end-market demand cycles.

Navitas Semiconductor.role: Fabless GaN/SiC power-semiconductor supplier targeting AI data-center power delivery; small, pre-profit, and competing against larger power-IC incumbents, so it sits as a speculative disruptive name with high beta and elevated terminal-drawdown risk despite a credible NVIDIA-linked design-win narrat

Cirrus Logic.role: Fabless designer of audio codecs and mixed-signal ICs heavily concentrated in smartphone customers (notably Apple); sits as a quality mid-cap with moderate moat but cyclical consumer-device exposure and high customer concentration limiting durability.

Synopsys.role: Synopsys is a dominant EDA and IP vendor whose recurring, design-cycle-embedded software makes it a durable semiconductor toolchain duopolist, hence low permanence risk and high moat.

Cadence Design Systems.role: Cadence is a duopoly leader in electronic design automation software and IP essential for designing advanced AI and semiconductor chips; its recurring, mission-critical software revenue and high switching costs make it a durable, moaty AI-infrastructure enabler rather than a cyclical hardware play.

Keysight Technologies.role: Keysight provides high-end electronic test and measurement instruments and software across communications, semiconductor, aerospace/defense and automotive markets; it holds a strong moat in precision T&M but carries exposure to cyclical R&D/capex budgets, placing it as a quality AI-infra adjacent na

Impinj.role: Impinj is the leading provider of RAIN RFID tags and reader ICs for item-level tracking in retail, logistics, and supply chains; it sits in disruptive with moderate permanence due to its endpoint IC dominance but cyclical, inventory-sensitive demand and only a tangential AI connection.

Wolfspeed peer / Aehr skip / Amtech.role: Small-cap maker of thermal processing and reflow/horizontal-diffusion equipment for semiconductor and SiC/power markets; sits in AI-infra peripherally but is a sub-$100M-revenue, cyclical, low-moat supplier with modest single-digit growth and high sensitivity to capex cycles.

Digital Turbine.role: Mobile app delivery and on-device media platform monetizing via carrier/OEM app preloads and ad placement; it sits in disruptive with high beta because revenue has been declining/flat, margins are thin, its moat is modest, and ad/app-install spend is cyclical and advertiser-discretionary.

ServiceTitan peer / Klaviyo skip / Yext.role: Yext provides digital presence and AI-driven search/answer management for brands, but flat-to-negative revenue and a crowded, fragmented market cap its moat and growth credibility despite the AI-search framing.

BigBear.ai.role: Small-cap provider of AI-driven decision intelligence for defense and government customers; sits in disruptive with high permanence risk due to tiny revenue, near-flat growth, persistent unprofitability, weak moat, and heavy reliance on lumpy government contracts.

Credo peer / Lightwave Logic.role: Pre-revenue developer of electro-optic polymer materials for high-speed optical modulators targeting AI/datacenter interconnect; speculative single-name with unproven commercialization and negligible revenue, hence high beta and terminal-risk loading.

Infinera skip / Applied Signal.role: ADTN (ADTRAN) supplies fiber access, optical transport and networking equipment to telecom/broadband carriers; it sits as a cyclical, carrier-capex-dependent infrastructure name with modest moat and uneven profitability, giving it mid growth and elevated terminal risk.

Extreme Networks.role: Enterprise networking vendor (wired/wireless LAN, cloud-managed switching) riding AI/edge networking demand, but a smaller fragmented-market player competing against Cisco/Arista/HPE with modest growth and cyclical enterprise IT spending exposure.

Juniper Networks.role: Enterprise and data-center networking vendor leveraging AI-driven switching/routing and Mist AIOps, but a secondary player behind Cisco/Arista with modest growth and cyclical enterprise capex exposure; pending HPE acquisition further caps independent upside.

Pure peer / NetApp.role: NetApp is a mature enterprise storage vendor benefiting from AI data-pipeline demand and all-flash/cloud transitions; it sits as a quality mid-cap with modest growth, solid recurring revenue, but faces competitive pressure from Pure Storage, Dell, and hyperscaler-native storage.

Western Digital peer / Sandisk.role: Sandisk is a pure-play NAND flash and SSD maker spun from Western Digital, supplying enterprise and AI-datacenter storage; it sits in AI-infra but with cyclical commodity-memory economics, modest pricing power in an oligopoly, and high sensitivity to the NAND boom-bust capex cycle.

Twilio.role: Twilio provides programmable messaging/voice APIs and is layering AI-driven customer-engagement tools; it sits in AI-platform with moderate growth given a maturing CPaaS core, recurring usage-based revenue, but faces competition and commoditization pressure that cap its moat.

Bentley Systems.role: Engineering software leader for infrastructure design and operations with recurring subscription revenue and a strong niche moat; sits defensive due to sticky ARR and non-discretionary infrastructure spend, though growth is modest and valuation is premium.

PTC.role: PTC provides PLM, CAD and IoT software (Windchill, Creo, Onshape) for industrial and manufacturing customers, with high recurring ARR; it sits as a quality defensive software name because its subscription base is sticky and non-discretionary, though AI upside is incremental rather than transformatio

Procore Technologies.role: Vertical SaaS leader for construction project management now layering AI features; recurring subscriptions give durability but exposure to cyclical construction spend and modest profitability place it in high-beta disruptive territory.

Amdocs peer / Pegasystems.role: Pegasystems sells BPM/CRM low-code automation software now transitioning to subscription and infusing generative AI; flat-to-declining revenue and modest moat in a fragmented enterprise-software market place it as a mid-quality AI-platform laggard with recurring but contestable revenue.

UiPath.role: UiPath is a leading RPA/agentic automation software vendor with recurring subscription revenue but decelerating growth (~3% YoY) and intensifying competition from Microsoft and AI-native agents, placing it as a mid-quality platform name with a contested moat.

nCino.role: nCino provides cloud-based operating and AI-enabled software for financial institutions; recurring SaaS revenue and entrenched bank workflows give durability, but modest growth, competitive lending/onboarding software markets, and bank IT budget sensitivity cap its moat and upside.

Appian.role: Low-code process automation vendor adding AI agents to workflows; decelerating ~4% growth, thin profitability, and a crowded competitive field (ServiceNow, Pega, Microsoft) cap its moat and justify a mid-tier quality/permanence profile.

Comfort peer / API Group.role: APG is a diversified safety and specialty services provider (inspection, fire/life-safety, specialty contracting) with modest exposure to data-center buildout and maintenance; its recurring, non-discretionary service base makes it a defensive, lower-beta play rather than a pure AI-infra growth name.

Quanta Services.role: Leading specialty infrastructure contractor for electric power transmission, distribution, and renewables; a credible picks-and-shovels beneficiary of AI data-center power demand, but revenue is project-based and sensitive to utility capex cycles and financing conditions.

EMCOR Group.role: Mechanical/electrical construction contractor benefiting from data-center buildout; cyclical project-based revenue tied to capex cycles makes earnings less durable than recurring-revenue peers.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker supplying power distribution, UPS, and switchgear for data centers; sits in AI-infra as a credible picks-and-shovels beneficiary of data-center buildout, though a large share of revenue remains tied to broader industrial and cyclical end-markets.

GE Vernova.role: Leading supplier of gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification hardware benefiting from surging datacenter power demand; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels play but with cyclical capex exposure and long project cycles tempering durability.

Powell Industries.role: Powell makes custom electrical switchgear and power control systems for utility, industrial, oil/gas and increasingly data-center customers; it benefits indirectly from AI-driven power buildout but remains a cyclical, project-based equipment maker with lumpy, capex-dependent demand.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small fast-spectrum nuclear reactors targeting data-center and industrial power; sits in disruptive with high permanence risk given no deployed units, long regulatory/build timelines, and valuation driven entirely by future AI-power demand narrative.

Centrus Energy.role: Centrus enriches uranium and is the sole U.S.-licensed HALEU producer for advanced reactors, giving it strategic leverage on energy/nuclear demand but with lumpy revenue, policy dependence, and cyclical fuel-contract timing that keep durability and moat moderate.

Hut 8.role: Bitcoin miner repurposing energy/data-center infrastructure toward AI/HPC compute hosting; speculative, crypto-levered, and capex-cyclical with an unproven AI transition, hence high beta and low durability.

ARKK (ARK Innovation).role: disruptive-innovation basket LED BY TESLA (~10%), then AMD, CRISPR, Tempus AI, Robinhood. High beta, rich multiples, Tesla-driven idiosyncratic swings — NOT a semis basket.

QQQ (Nasdaq-100).role: Nasdaq-100 mega-cap tech; quality, but rich and tech-tilted.

VOO (S&P 500).role: broad US large-cap; the market itself — durable, diversified.

SCHD (Dividend).role: quality-dividend value basket; low beta, cheap, durable earnings.

DTCR (Data Ctr Infra).role: data-center REITs & digital infra (Equinix, Digital Realty, American Tower); physical, contracted, durable — low beta.

GRID (Smart Grid).role: grid/power equipment for the AI electricity demand (Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova); inelastic infra spend.

NUKE (Nuclear/Uranium).role: nuclear/uranium for data-center baseload (Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, BWX); high-growth but cyclical/volatile.

VGT (Info Tech).role: broad US information-technology sector; mega-cap heavy, durable.

IGV (Software).role: application & infrastructure software basket; higher multiple, subscription-durable.
